codeReview.summary: Clean, well-structured implementation of error injection for MockTransport. Two new Optional<TransportError> fields added to the struct, with setter methods and one-shot (auto-clear via .take()) semantics in the Transport impl. Three tests cover write error injection+recovery, read error injection+recovery (preserving queued data), and read error returning Err. All changes are properly gated behind the std feature (the entire mock module is #[cfg(feature = "std")]).

issues.description: The doc comments say 'Inject an error to be returned by the next write()/read() call' and 'Pass None to clear a previously set error'. However, the auto-clear behavior (via .take()) is a one-shot mechanism that is not explicitly documented. A consumer might expect the error to persist until explicitly cleared. The handoff clarifies this is intentional (one-shot), but the doc comment could be more explicit about this. Minor — does not affect correctness.

test_mock_transport_read_error_returns_zero_bytes is somewhat redundant with test_mock_transport_read_error_injection_and_recovery. Both test read error injection — the difference is that one uses TransportError::Timeout vs TransportError::Io, and the 'zero bytes' test does not inject data beforehand. This is fine for coverage clarity, just noting the overlap.

summary: PASS. The implementation fully satisfies VAL-HAL-001 (write error injection with recovery test) and VAL-HAL-002 (read error injection with recovery test). Both assertion requirements are met: (1) at least 1 test configures MockTransport to return error on write, verifies error, verifies recovery — done in test_mock_transport_write_error_injection_and_recovery; (2) at least 1 test configures read error injection, verifies error, verifies recovery — done in test_mock_transport_read_error_injection_and_recovery and test_mock_transport_read_error_returns_zero_bytes. The implementation is properly gated behind #[cfg(feature = "std")] (the entire mock module). The one-shot auto-clear behavior is a clean design choice. Production code changes are limited to test-only infrastructure (MockTransport is only used in tests). Code quality is high — follows existing patterns, clean assertions, no unsafe blocks added.
